body: The case for depth: three-way contests carried the Kandinsky ($74m hammer against $60–80m) and Phillips’s Modigliani head ($38.2m against $28–35m). Phillips made $104.4m, up 55% on last year. Sotheby’s Modern sale landed within its $260.2–378.4m estimate, with 11 lots above their high estimates and records for Cassatt and Aaron Douglas. The Baum collection sold all 24 lots within its estimate.

The case against: the most expensive works sold at or under their guides. The Van Gogh and the Cézanne Arlequin ($99m hammer against about $120m) both fell short, and six of the twelve Blaquier-Arrieta lots sold below their low estimates. Christie’s 20th Century sale hammered at $521m, the low end of $511–743m, after withdrawals; the Koons Le Baiser sold below its estimate. At Sotheby’s, a third of the Baum lots and a third of the Modern lots sold below their low estimates.

The guarantees did their job, which is not the same as demand. A guarantee fixes the seller’s price; the Van Gogh sold to a single room bidder below its guide, so the record is real but the depth is not proven. Read the season by the lots that drew more than one bidder past the guarantee: the Kandinsky, the Modigliani, the Magritte, the Rivera. The settlement with the Fischer heirs, reached hours before the sale, shows restitution risk is now priced in at the last minute, not discovered after.

The last night settled the question the desk set on Thursday. Christie’s 21st Century sale was about 59% guaranteed, and its top lots sold to guarantors or single bidders at or under their low estimates: the Basquiat at $28m hammer, the Lichtenstein Large Spool at $7m against $10–15m. Fresh, cheaply estimated works did better: the Hilma af Klint made 16 times its high estimate in Stockholm, and the Nara at Fair Warning drew four bidders. The money is there for the rare thing at a modest guide; it is not there for the full estimate on the familiar thing.
change: If the December sales in London and Abu Dhabi clear their low estimates with contested lots, the spring will fill with consignments at lower guides. If they too sell to guarantors at or below the lows, estimates will have to fall and guarantee capacity will shrink.
dek: The week of 16–20 November made about $2.44bn, up from $2.23bn, with records for Van Gogh ($190.4m) and Kandinsky ($85.8m). But the Van Gogh hammered below its guide, the Blaquier-Arrieta collection made $358m at hammer against about $450m, and Christie’s 21st Century sale closed the week at $117.7m hammer against a $126–192m estimate, its $30–50m Basquiat selling under its low.
h: New York made about $2.44bn, but the top lots sold to few bidders and the week closed below estimate.
